title: Team Rhythm demo questions and expected answer behaviour
status: Authored examples for testing; not recorded model outputs
rules: Use only the specified source scope for each question.
Cite dated sources and distinguish facts, calculations, inference and missing evidence.
Best supported answer means useful supported detail with uncertainty, not an invented owner, date or reason.
Latest recorded status is not proof of a present-day outcome when updates are missing.
Do not invent numeric confidence scores or treat recommendations as saved commitments.

questions.question: Who originally agreed to finish the onboarding guide, and by when?
questions.expected_answer: Alex agreed on 25 September to finish the onboarding guide by 2 October 2026. Sam recorded the agreement; Alex owns the task.

evidence.excerpt: Commitment: Alex will finish the onboarding guide by 2 October 2026.

must_not_claim: Sam is the task owner
The original agreement was due 5 October

Meeting ratings: Alex 9/10, Sam 9/10.

questions.question: How often did Alex and Sam miss their targets, and by how much?
questions.expected_answer: Both missed in two of four weeks, or 50%. Alex was short by two enquiries on 11 September and one on 18 September: an average shortfall of 1.5 enquiries across the missed weeks. Sam was one hour over on 11 September and two hours over on 25 September: an average excess of 1.5 hours across the missed weeks. These are different measures, so their gap sizes should not be combined.

evidence.excerpt: Signals: Alex, qualified enquiries, actual 8, target at least 10 enquiries.
Signals: Alex, qualified enquiries, actual 9, target at least 10 enquiries.
Signals: Sam, median response time, actual 5, target at most 4 hours.
Signals: Sam, median response time, actual 6, target at most 4 hours.

must_not_claim: Lower response time is a miss
A combined average gap in enquiries and hours
Target misses prove individual underperformance

questions.question: Which issue keeps coming back?
questions.expected_answer: Unclear handoffs appears in three of four meetings: 11, 18 and 25 September. Friday cover appears in two: 18 September and 2 October. Counts are distinct meetings, not repeated mentions.

evidence.excerpt: Issue: Unclear handoffs. Requests had no named next owner.

questions.question: What is most likely slowing the team down?
questions.expected_answer: Unclear handoffs is the strongest recurring concern in these records, appearing in three of four meetings. It is a sensible place to investigate first, but the records do not prove it caused the missed targets or the guide's delay.

evidence.excerpt: Issue: Unclear handoffs. Requests had no named next owner.
Issue: Unclear handoffs. The gap raised on 11 September remained open.
Issue: Unclear handoffs, raised for the third meeting.

questions.required_uncertainty: Label the bottleneck suggestion as an inference; causal evidence is absent.
must_not_claim: Handoffs definitely caused the delays
Alex or Sam is to blame

questions.expected_answer: A useful starting point is to review the onboarding guide and the handoff process: the guide was still open in the latest meeting, and handoffs appeared in three meetings. This is a suggested agenda focus, not a new agreed commitment.

Commitment carried forward: onboarding guide, owner Alex, due 5 October 2026.

questions.question: Which actions are clear enough to save, and which need a question first?
questions.expected_answer: There are seven distinct agreed actions. Five have an identifiable owner and deadline: Alex's handover guide, Sam's checklist, Morgan's case study, Jo's referral export and Casey's testimonial clips. Sam's welcome-email refresh needs a deadline. The cover rota has a deadline of 12 October but its owner is inaudible. Review the five clear actions before saving, and clarify the other two.

evidence.excerpt: We haven't picked a deadline.
[overlapping speech; owner name inaudible]: I'll do the rota.

must_not_claim: 5/7 is measured AI accuracy
The repeated video upload is an eighth task
The podcast is an agreed task
